source.diagram: MgO-SiO2 phase diagram based mainly on the results of Bowen, Andersen [1], Smyth [2], Henriksen, Kingery [3], Henney, Jones [4] and Hageman, Oonk [5]
source.caption: Atlas text (printed p. 88): 'Contrary to previous results by Schlaudt, Roy [6], no solubility of SiO2 in MgO was reported by Henney, Jones [4] and Henriksen, Kingery [3]. The polymorphism in MgO·SiO2 has been investigated by Foster [7], Atlas [8], Sarver, Hummel [9] and Smyth [2]. The miscibility gap in the system MgO-SiO2 has been investigated by Greig [10], Olshansky [11] and recently by Hageman, Oonk [5]. The critical temperature reported by Hageman, Oonk [5], which is considerably below the previous reported values, has been adopted. The recent investigations of liquidus relations at 1600 and 1700 °C by Kambayashi, Kato [12, 13] (dashed line in the figure) suggest congruent melting of MgO·SiO2.' References: [1] N. L. Bowen, O. Andersen, Am. J. Sci., 4th Ser. 37 (1914) No. 222, 487/501; [2] J. R. Smyth, Am. Mineral. 59 (1974) 345/52; [3] A. F. Henriksen, W. D. Kingery, Ceramurgia Int. 5 (1979) No. 1, 11/7; [4] J. W. Henney, J. W. S. Jones, Trans. J. Br. Ceram. Soc. 68 (1969) 201/3; [5] V. B. Hageman, H. A. Oonk, Phys. Chem. Glasses 27 (1986) No. 5, 194/8; [6] C. M. Schlaudt, D. M. Roy, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 48 (1965) No. 5, 248/51; [7] W. R. Foster, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 34 (1951) No. 9, 255/9; [8] L. Atlas, J. Geol. 60 (1952) 125/47; [9] J. F. Sarver, F. A. Hummel, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 45 (1962) No. 4, 152/6; [10] J. W. Greig, Am. J. Sci., 5th Ser. 13 (1927) No. 73, 1/154; [11] Ya. I. Olshansky, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 76 (1951) No. 1, 94/6; [12] S. Kambayashi, E. Kato, J. Chem. Thermodyn. 15 (1983) No. 8, 701/7; [13] S. Kambayashi, E. Kato, J. Chem. Thermodyn. 16 (1984) No. 3, 241/8.

nbsCrossCheck.result: No MgO-SiO2 binary entry. The system index (PDF p. 140, printed p. 132) lists MgO-Sc2O3 followed by MgO-SiO2-SrO; no Mg2SiO4-MgSiO3 or MgSiO3-SiO2 join either. All values below are atlas-only (status 'extracted').

digitization.method: Liquidus and miscibility gap traced along the stroke centre, column by column (row by row on the steep SiO2-side branch); invariant lines from the horizontal strokes.
digitization.check: Compound lines at 42.7 and 59.9 wt% SiO2 (stoichiometric Mg2SiO4 42.7, MgSiO3 59.9). Invariant lines read 1849 / 1556 / 1541 / 1695 / 1468.5 °C (labels 1850 / 1557 / 1543 / 1695 / 1470). Forsterite maximum 1887 °C (label 1890); periclase liquidus meets the MgO axis at 2830 °C (label 2822); cristobalite liquidus meets the SiO2 axis at 1725 °C (label 1725). Digitized vs printed composition labels: 61.2 / '61', 63.4 / '64', but 39.3 / '38' and 68.9 / '70' wt% SiO2 (drawn ≈1.2 wt% from the label).

liquidusSource.read: digitized stroke centre; end points set to the printed invariant and melting-point labels (2822, 1850 at 38, 1890, 1557 at 61, 1543 at 64, 1695 at 70, 1725). Digitized points within 1.5 wt% of the junctions drawn away from their labels (38, 70) are omitted. The enstatite branch is a short segment between the two invariants; the silica branch is flat at the monotectic between 70 and 98.9 wt% SiO2.
